lodging.name: The Cliff House at Pikes Peak

founded.text: Founded as a resort community. The National Register nomination names Dr. William Bell as the town's founder.

timeline.text: The first passenger train reached the summit of Pikes Peak on the cog railway on June 30.
Father Jean Baptiste Francolon, the architect of Miramont Castle, moved to Manitou Springs for his health.
Historic Manitou Springs, Inc. was formed as a nonprofit.
The Manitou Springs Heritage Museum opened on the first floor of 517 Manitou Avenue.

sites.name: Manitou Springs Heritage Museum
sites.hours: Wednesday–Sunday noon–4 pm or by appointment

sites.name: Miramont Castle
sites.hours: Tuesday–Sunday 10 am–3:30 pm, closing at 4 pm; Memorial Day to Labor Day, daily 9 am–4:30 pm, closing at 5 pm
sites.cost: Adults 13–59 $15; seniors 60+ $13; children 4–12 $10; 3 and under free

sites.name: Manitou Cliff Dwellings
sites.hours: May–August 9 am–5 pm; April, September and October 9 am–5 pm; March 9 am–4:30 pm; November 9 am–4 pm; December–February 10 am–4 pm
sites.cost: Adults (12 and over) $12.75 plus tax; children (4–11) $8; seniors (60 plus) $10; 3 and under free
sites.season: Open year-round, weather permitting; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day

sites.name: The Broadmoor Manitou and Pikes Peak Cog Railway
sites.cost: Reserved admission booked online: adults starting at $67; children starting at $57

trails.name: Manitou Incline
trails.length: About 1 mile up, with about 2,000 feet of climbing; down by Barr Trail, never by the steps
trails.trailhead: The base, at the upper end of Ruxton Avenue; Route 33, the free shuttle, stops at The Incline/Cog Railway
trails.season: All year: 6 am–6 pm from May through October, 6 am–3 pm from November through April.
trails.fee: A free reservation and a signed waiver for every climb, for parties of up to eight; booked on the City’s Incline page.

trails.name: Garden of the Gods Park
trails.manager: City of Colorado Springs, with the Garden of the Gods Visitor & Nature Center
trails.size: More than 22 miles of trail; the Perkins Central Garden Trail is an easy 1.5-mile round trip with less than 30 feet of rise
trails.address: Visitor & Nature Center, 1805 N. 30th Street, Colorado Springs
trails.season: Daily, 5 am–9 pm from November 1 to April 30 and 5 am–10 pm from May 1 to October 31. The Visitor Center is closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s Day.
trails.dogs: On a 6-foot leash at all times; pick up after them.
trails.fee: Free: the park was given to the city in 1909 on condition it stay free.

trails.name: Barr Trail
trails.kind: National forest trail to Pikes Peak
trails.manager: U.S. Forest Service, Pikes Peak Ranger District
trails.length: 12 miles to the summit, climbing from 6,647 to 14,091 feet; the Forest says an average hiker needs about 16 hours for the round trip
trails.trailhead: Off Ruxton Avenue above the Pikes Peak Cog Railway depot; the free Manitou Shuttle’s Route 33 stops at Barr Trail
trails.fee: A fee to park at the trailhead.
